name: peft

members.name: PeftConfig
members.signature: PeftConfig(task_type: TaskType | str | None = None, peft_type: PeftType | str | None = None, auto_mapping: dict[str, str] | None = None, base_model_name_or_path: str | None = None, revision: str | None = None, inference_mode: bool = False)

methods.name: to_dict
methods.summary: Return the config as the JSON-ready dict `adapter_config.json` holds.
methods.extended:
Enums become their strings and sets of module names sorted lists,
so the result goes straight to `json.dumps` and back through
`from_dict`.

returns.description: One entry per field, keyed by the reference's field names.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig
>>> d = LoraConfig(target_modules=["v", "q"], task_type="CAUSAL_LM").to_dict()
>>> d["target_modules"], d["task_type"], d["peft_type"]
(['q', 'v'], 'CAUSAL_LM', 'LORA')

methods.name: from_dict
methods.summary: Build a config from a dict such as a parsed `adapter_config.json`.
methods.extended:
The constructor cannot do this: a file from the reference carries
keys v1 has no field for.  Such a key is accepted only at a value
that turns its feature off — null, false or empty
(`"lora_bias": false`, `"loftq_config": {}`) — and dropped (with
a warning if v1 does not know the key); at any other value it
raises, as it would change what the adapter computes.  The
`peft_version` provenance key is dropped.  Called on
`PeftConfig`, the dict's `peft_type` picks the class.

parameters.name: config_dict
parameters.description: The config's fields, by the reference's names.

returns.description: The validated config, of the class the dict's method names.

raises.description:
The dict describes another adapter type, or turns on a feature
v1 lacks.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig
>>> config = LoraConfig.from_dict(
...     {"peft_type": "LORA", "r": 4, "target_modules": ["c_attn"],
...      "use_dora": False, "loftq_config": {}, "peft_version": "0.17.0"})
>>> config.r, config.target_modules
(4, {'c_attn'})

methods.name: save_pretrained
methods.summary: Write `adapter_config.json` into `save_directory`.
methods.extended:
The file is the reference's: `to_dict` with its keys sorted,
indented by two spaces.  The directory is created if missing.

parameters.name: save_directory
parameters.description: Directory to write into.

raises.description: `save_directory` names an existing file.

examples:
>>> import tempfile
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["fc"]).save_pretrained(d)
...     LoraConfig.from_pretrained(d).r
2

methods.name: from_json_file
methods.summary: Read a config file into the dict it holds, unchanged but for `runtime_config`.
methods.extended:
What `from_pretrained` reads before it chooses a config class: the
file's content as a dict, as the reference's `from_json_file` returns
it.  `from_dict` turns it into a config.

parameters.name: path_json_file
parameters.description: The path of a JSON file such as `adapter_config.json`.

returns.description:
The file's object, without a `runtime_config` key: the
reference warns that such a key is ignored, since a runtime
configuration is valid at runtime only.

raises.description: There is no file at `path_json_file`.
The file does not hold a JSON object.

examples:
>>> import os, tempfile
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, PeftConfig
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["fc"]).save_pretrained(d)
...     raw = PeftConfig.from_json_file(os.path.join(d, "adapter_config.json"))
>>> raw["peft_type"], raw["r"]
('LORA', 2)

methods.name: from_pretrained
methods.signature: from_pretrained(pretrained_model_name_or_path: str | os.PathLike[str], subfolder: str | None = None)
methods.summary: Read `adapter_config.json` from a local adapter directory.
methods.extended:
The file's `peft_type` picks the config class: called on
`PeftConfig` this returns a `LoraConfig` for a LoRA adapter,
and called on a method's own class it refuses the file of another
method.

parameters.name: pretrained_model_name_or_path
parameters.description:
A directory holding `adapter_config.json` — one written by
`save_pretrained` or by the reference library.  Hub ids
are not resolved; download the adapter first.

parameters.name: subfolder
parameters.description:
A directory under `pretrained_model_name_or_path` that holds
the file, e.g. the sub-directory `save_pretrained` gives each
adapter but the one named `"default"`.

raises.description: The directory has no `adapter_config.json`.
The file does not hold a JSON object.

examples:
>>> import tempfile
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     LoraConfig(r=16, lora_alpha=32, target_modules="all-linear").save_pretrained(d)
...     loaded = LoraConfig.from_pretrained(d)
>>> loaded.r, loaded.lora_alpha, loaded.target_modules
(16, 32, 'all-linear')

methods.name: __init__
methods.signature: __init__(task_type: TaskType | str | None = None, peft_type: PeftType | str | None = None, auto_mapping: dict[str, str] | None = None, base_model_name_or_path: str | None = None, revision: str | None = None, inference_mode: bool = False)

members.summary: What every adapter config holds, and the `adapter_config.json` round trip.
members.extended:
The base of each method's config (`LoraConfig`), with the fields
the reference's `PeftConfig` has.  Called on `PeftConfig` itself,
`from_pretrained` / `from_dict` read the method the file names and
return that method's config — the reference's idiom for learning which
base model an adapter needs before loading either.  It is not built
directly: a config of no method adapts nothing.

parameters.name: task_type
parameters.description: The task the adapter is for (metadata; see `TaskType`).

parameters.name: peft_type
parameters.description:
The method; filled in by the subclass when omitted, refused when
it names another.

parameters.name: auto_mapping
parameters.description:
The class of the base model, `{"base_model_class": name,
"parent_library": module}` — what `AutoPeftModel*` rebuilds the
base with.  `PeftModel.save_pretrained` writes it.

parameters.name: base_model_name_or_path
parameters.description: Name of the model the adapter was trained on (metadata).

parameters.name: revision
parameters.description: Revision of that model (metadata).

parameters.name: inference_mode
parameters.description: Freeze the adapter too, for inference.

raises.description: Built directly, or a field holds a value of the wrong type.

examples:
>>> import tempfile
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, PeftConfig
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     LoraConfig(target_modules=["q"], base_model_name_or_path="gpt2").save_pretrained(d)
...     config = PeftConfig.from_pretrained(d)
>>> type(config).__name__, config.base_model_name_or_path
('LoraConfig', 'gpt2')

members.name: PeftType
members.signature: PeftType()
members.summary: The parameter-efficient method an adapter file holds.
members.extended:
The members are the reference library's `peft_type` strings, so a
config file names its method the same way on both sides.
`lucid.peft` implements `LORA`; reading a file of any other
type raises `NotImplementedError`.

members.name: TaskType
members.signature: TaskType()
members.summary: The task an adapter was trained for, as `adapter_config.json` records it.
members.extended:
It chooses the model class `lucid.peft.get_peft_model` and
`PeftModel.from_pretrained` return: `PeftModelForCausalLM` for
`CAUSAL_LM` and so on (`MODEL_TYPE_TO_PEFT_MODEL_MAPPING`), a plain
`PeftModel` for an adapter with no task.  A classification or
question-answering wrapper makes the model's head trainable when it
has one under the reference's conventional name (`classifier` /
`score`, `qa_outputs`).

members.name: get_peft_model
members.signature: get_peft_model(model: nn.Module, peft_config: PeftConfig, adapter_name: str = 'default')
members.summary: Adapt `model` with LoRA and return it wrapped as a `lucid.peft.PeftModel`.
members.extended:
The model is changed in place: each module `peft_config` selects
becomes a LoRA layer around the original, and every parameter but the
adapter's is frozen.  `peft_config` is not changed — the wrapper
keeps a copy — with two additions the reference makes too: a
`base_model_name_or_path` read from the model's `name_or_path`,
when it has one, and, for a classification or question-answering
`task_type`, the model's `classifier` / `score` / `qa_outputs`
head added to `modules_to_save` so that it trains.

The class returned follows `peft_config.task_type`:
`PeftModelForCausalLM` for `"CAUSAL_LM"`, `PeftModelForSeq2SeqLM`,
`PeftModelForSequenceClassification`, `PeftModelForTokenClassification`,
`PeftModelForQuestionAnswering` and `PeftModelForFeatureExtraction`
for theirs (`MODEL_TYPE_TO_PEFT_MODEL_MAPPING` is the table), and a
plain `PeftModel` when the config has no task.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description:
The model to adapt — any module; a zoo model keeps its
`generate` and heads through the wrapper.

parameters.name: peft_config
parameters.description: What to adapt and how — a `LoraConfig`; its method picks the tuner.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: Name of the adapter, the key in every `lora_A` / `lora_B`.

raises.description: `peft_config` is not an adapter config.

No module matches `target_modules`, or a match is not an
`nn.Linear`.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(16, 16), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(16, 4))
>>> peft = get_peft_model(net, LoraConfig(r=4, lora_alpha=8, target_modules=["0", "2"]))
>>> peft.print_trainable_parameters()
trainable params: 208 || all params: 548 || trainable%: 37.9562
>>> peft(lucid.randn(2, 16)).shape
(2, 4)

members.name: inject_adapter_in_model
members.signature: inject_adapter_in_model(peft_config: PeftConfig, model: nn.Module, adapter_name: str = 'default')
members.summary: Put LoRA layers into `model` in place and return it, without a wrapper.
members.extended:
For code that manages the model itself: the model is adapted and
frozen exactly as by `lucid.peft.get_peft_model`, but returned
bare, so its state dict keeps its own key names (plus `base_layer` /
`lora_A` / `lora_B` under each adapted layer).
`lucid.peft.get_peft_model_state_dict` reads the adapter out
of it.  Note the argument order, the reference's: config first.

parameters.name: peft_config
parameters.description: What to adapt and how — a `LoraConfig`.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: The model to adapt.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: Name of the adapter.

examples:
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, inject_adapter_in_model
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 4), nn.Linear(4, 2))
>>> inject_adapter_in_model(LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["1"]), net) is net
True
>>> sorted(net.state_dict())
['0.bias', '0.weight', '1.base_layer.bias', '1.base_layer.weight', '1.lora_A.default.weight', '1.lora_B.default.weight']

members.name: PeftModel
members.signature: PeftModel(model: nn.Module, peft_config: PeftConfig, adapter_name: str = 'default')

methods.name: peft_config
methods.summary: Each adapter's config by adapter name (`"all-linear"` spelled out).

methods.name: active_adapter
methods.summary: Name of the adapter in use (a list once `delete_adapter` leaves several or none).

methods.name: active_adapters
methods.summary: The adapters in use, as a list.

methods.name: get_base_model
methods.summary: Return the adapted model itself — the one passed in, now holding LoRA layers.

methods.name: add_adapter
methods.signature: add_adapter(adapter_name: str, peft_config: PeftConfig, low_cpu_mem_usage: bool = False)
methods.summary: Add an adapter beside the ones the model holds.
methods.extended:
The new adapter is initialised, not trained, and starts frozen and
inactive: the model computes what it computed, and every parameter
keeps its `requires_grad`.  Switch to it with `set_adapter`.
Modules an earlier adapter wraps take the new one beside it; a
classification or question-answering `task_type` adds the model's
head to `modules_to_save` as `get_peft_model` does.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: Name of the new adapter; unique among the model's adapters.

parameters.name: peft_config
parameters.description: What to adapt and how.

parameters.name: low_cpu_mem_usage
parameters.description:
Accepted for the reference's signature; the adapter is built
the same way either way.

raises.description:
The name is taken, the config is another method's, no module
matches it, or two adapters would train biases.  The model is
left as it was.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 4), nn.Linear(4, 2))
>>> peft = get_peft_model(net, LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"]))
>>> peft.add_adapter("second", LoraConfig(r=4, target_modules=["0", "1"]))
>>> peft.active_adapter, sorted(peft.peft_config)
('default', ['default', 'second'])
>>> peft.set_adapter("second")
>>> peft.get_base_model()[1].lora_A["second"].weight.shape
(4, 4)

methods.name: set_adapter
methods.summary: Make `adapter_name` the adapter in use.
methods.extended:
Only the one adapter applies.  It trains, and every other adapter is
frozen, unless `inference_mode`.  A merged model is unmerged
first; layers that hold nothing of the adapter run their base alone.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: An adapter the model holds.

parameters.name: inference_mode
parameters.description: Freeze the adapter too.

raises.description: The model has no adapter of that name.

methods.name: delete_adapter
methods.summary: Remove an adapter, its config and its `modules_to_save` copies from the model.
methods.extended:
If it was the one in use, the first of the others (by name) takes
over, with a warning.  Deleting the last adapter leaves a model
that applies nothing; `unload()` takes the layers out.

raises.description: The model has no adapter of that name, or it is merged.

methods.name: set_requires_grad
methods.signature: set_requires_grad(adapter_names: str | Sequence[str], requires_grad: bool = True)
methods.summary: Enable or disable gradients on the named adapter(s), leaving the rest as they are.

parameters.name: adapter_names
parameters.description: The adapter, or adapters, to change.

parameters.name: requires_grad
parameters.description: Whether they train.

raises.description: A name is not one of the model's adapters.

methods.name: get_nb_trainable_parameters
methods.summary: Return `(trainable, total)` parameter counts, each shared parameter once.

returns.description: Elements in parameters that require grad, and in all of them.

methods.name: print_trainable_parameters
methods.summary: Print the trainable / total parameter counts and their ratio.
examples:
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
>>> peft = get_peft_model(nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(8, 8)),
...                       LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"]))
>>> peft.print_trainable_parameters()
trainable params: 32 || all params: 104 || trainable%: 30.7692

methods.name: disable_adapter
methods.summary: Run the base model alone inside the `with` block.
methods.extended:
LoRA updates are skipped (a merged layer is unmerged on entry, and
stays unmerged after) and every `modules_to_save` module runs as
the original; the adapter comes back when the block exits, even on
an exception.  Blocks nest: the adapter stays off until the
outermost one exits.  Merging inside the block is refused.  A
compiled model follows the switch: the state it branches on is
part of its cache key.
examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 4))
>>> x = lucid.randn(2, 4)
>>> base_out = net(x)
>>> peft = get_peft_model(net, LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"],
...                                       init_lora_weights=False))
>>> with peft.disable_adapter():
...     bool((peft(x) == base_out).all().item())
True

methods.name: merge_and_unload
methods.signature: merge_and_unload(progressbar: bool = False, safe_merge: bool = False, adapter_names: list[str] | None = None)
methods.summary: Fold the adapter(s) into the base model and hand the base model back.
methods.extended:
For deployment: the result runs at the base model's cost and saves,
exports and compiles as an ordinary model.  This wrapper is spent
afterwards, and adapters that were not folded in are gone with it.

parameters.name: progressbar
parameters.description: Kept for call compatibility with the reference; ignored.

parameters.name: safe_merge
parameters.description:
Refuse, before changing any weight, if a merged weight would
hold NaN or inf.

parameters.name: adapter_names
parameters.description: Which adapters to fold in; the ones in use by default.

raises.description:
A base weight is shared with another module (a tied head),
or a `modules_to_save` module was trained apart from a tie.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
>>> peft = get_peft_model(nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 2)),
...                       LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"], init_lora_weights=False))
>>> x = lucid.randn(3, 4)
>>> adapted = peft(x)
>>> plain = peft.merge_and_unload()
>>> type(plain[0]) is nn.Linear, bool(lucid.allclose(plain(x), adapted, atol=1e-5))
(True, True)

methods.name: unload
methods.summary: Remove the adapter without merging and return the original model.

returns.description: The model, each LoRA layer replaced by the `nn.Linear` it wrapped.

methods.name: save_pretrained
methods.signature: save_pretrained(save_directory: str | os.PathLike[str], safe_serialization: bool = True, selected_adapters: list[str] | None = None)
methods.summary: Write the adapters — not the base model — under `save_directory`.
methods.extended:
Per adapter, the reference library's two files:
`adapter_config.json` (with `inference_mode` set, as the
reference stores it, and the base model's class as `auto_mapping`)
and `adapter_model.safetensors`, keyed by
`lucid.peft.get_peft_model_state_dict`.  The adapter named
`"default"` goes into `save_directory` itself, every other into
a sub-directory of its own name, as the reference lays it out; an
adapter is read back from the directory that holds its two files
(`PeftModel.from_pretrained` / `load_adapter`).

parameters.name: save_directory
parameters.description: Directory to write into; created if missing.

parameters.name: safe_serialization
parameters.description:
Must be `True`: the pickle format the reference writes for
`False` is not one Lucid can produce.

parameters.name: selected_adapters
parameters.description: The adapters to write; every adapter of the model by default.

raises.description: `safe_serialization=False`.
`selected_adapters` names an adapter the model lacks.

The adapters were merged or unloaded already — there is nothing
left to save; nothing is written.
`save_directory` names an existing file.

examples:
>>> import tempfile, os
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
>>> peft = get_peft_model(nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 2)),
...                       LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"]))
>>> peft.add_adapter("style", LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"]))
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     peft.save_pretrained(d)
...     sorted(os.listdir(d)), sorted(os.listdir(os.path.join(d, "style")))
(['adapter_config.json', 'adapter_model.safetensors', 'style'], ['adapter_config.json', 'adapter_model.safetensors'])

methods.name: from_pretrained
methods.signature: from_pretrained(model: nn.Module, model_id: str | os.PathLike[str], adapter_name: str = 'default', is_trainable: bool = False, config: PeftConfig | None = None, subfolder: str | None = None)
methods.summary: Adapt `model` with the adapter saved in `model_id`.
methods.extended:
Reads `adapter_config.json` (unless `config` is given) and
`adapter_model.safetensors` — written by `save_pretrained`
or by the reference library — injects the adapter into `model` in
place and loads its tensors.  If the tensors do not fit the model,
the injection is undone before the error is raised.  The class
returned follows the config's `task_type` as in
`lucid.peft.get_peft_model`; only an adapter with no task
is built as `cls`.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: The base model the adapter was trained on.

parameters.name: model_id
parameters.description: A local adapter directory.  Hub ids are not resolved.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: Name to give the adapter.

parameters.name: is_trainable
parameters.description:
Keep the adapter trainable.  By default it is frozen and the
model is put in `eval()` mode, for inference.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: Use this config instead of the directory's.

parameters.name: subfolder
parameters.description: The directory under `model_id` that holds the adapter.

returns.description:
`model`, adapted and loaded — a task wrapper if the adapter
names a task.

raises.description: The directory lacks `adapter_config.json` or the weights.

The weights are a pickle (`adapter_model.bin`), or the config
describes something lucid.peft does not implement.
The adapter's tensors do not fit `model`.

examples:
>>> import tempfile
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, PeftModel, get_peft_model
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 2))
>>> base_state = {k: v.clone() for k, v in net.state_dict().items()}
>>> trained = get_peft_model(net, LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"],
...                                         init_lora_weights=False))
>>> x = lucid.randn(3, 4)
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     trained.save_pretrained(d)
...     fresh = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 2))
...     _ = fresh.load_state_dict(base_state)
...     loaded = PeftModel.from_pretrained(fresh, d)
>>> bool(lucid.allclose(loaded(x), trained(x)))
True

methods.name: load_adapter
methods.signature: load_adapter(model_id: str | os.PathLike[str], adapter_name: str, is_trainable: bool = False, low_cpu_mem_usage: bool = False, subfolder: str | None = None)
methods.summary: Load a saved adapter into the model, beside the ones it holds.
methods.extended:
An adapter the model does not hold is added from the directory's
config and filled from its weights; the weights of one the model
already holds replace the values it has.  The loaded adapter is not
made the one in use — `set_adapter` does that.  Nothing changes
if the files are missing or their tensors do not fit.

parameters.name: model_id
parameters.description:
The local directory that holds the adapter's `adapter_config.json`
and `adapter_model.safetensors`; for an adapter saved by
`save_pretrained` beside others, that is its sub-directory.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: Name to give the adapter.

parameters.name: is_trainable
parameters.description:
Make the adapter trainable.  Otherwise it stays frozen and the
model is put in `eval()` mode, for inference.

parameters.name: low_cpu_mem_usage
parameters.description:
Accepted for the reference's signature; ignored as in
`add_adapter`.

parameters.name: subfolder
parameters.description: The directory under `model_id` that holds the adapter.

returns.description:
What `model.load_state_dict(..., strict=False)` returned, as
`set_peft_model_state_dict` hands it back.

raises.description: The directory lacks `adapter_config.json` or the weights.

The weights are a pickle, or the config describes something
lucid.peft does not implement.

The adapter's tensors do not fit the model, or its config cannot
sit beside the adapters held.

examples:
>>> import tempfile
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, PeftModel, get_peft_model
>>> config = LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"])
>>> source = get_peft_model(nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 2)), config)
>>> mine = get_peft_model(nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 2)), config)
>>> with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
...     source.save_pretrained(d)
...     _ = mine.load_adapter(d, "loaded")
>>> sorted(mine.peft_config), mine.active_adapter
(['default', 'loaded'], 'default')

members.summary: A model with adapters, saved and loaded as the adapters alone.
members.extended:
Wraps the model in its method's tuner (`LoraModel` for a
`LoraConfig`), kept as `base_model` (the user's model is
`base_model.model`), so the
state dict reads `base_model.model....lora_A.default.weight` and the
adapter file `base_model.model....lora_A.weight`, the reference
library's layouts.  Calling it runs the wrapped model, and any public
name it lacks — `generate`, `config`, a head — is read from that
model, so code written for the bare model keeps working.

The model holds any number of adapters by name.  `add_adapter` and
`load_adapter` bring one in beside the others (frozen and inactive),
`set_adapter` switches which one the model computes with — and
trains — and `delete_adapter` drops one.  `save_pretrained` writes
them all, the `"default"` one at the directory itself and each other
in a sub-directory of its own name.

Usually made by `lucid.peft.get_peft_model`, or by
`from_pretrained` for a saved adapter.  Both pick the class from the
config's `task_type`: the wrappers (`PeftModelForCausalLM` and the
others, `MODEL_TYPE_TO_PEFT_MODEL_MAPPING`) are subclasses of this
one, each registered for its task by `class Wrapper(PeftModel,
task_type=TaskType.X)`; an adapter with no task, or a task no wrapper
is registered for, gets this class itself.

parameters.name: model

members.summary: Return the adapter's tensors under the keys an adapter file uses.
members.extended:
That is `lora_A` / `lora_B` of every adapted layer, the trained
copy of every `modules_to_save` module and the biases `bias`
trains — keyed as the reference writes them, the adapter name taken
out.  Called on a `PeftModel` the keys start `base_model.model.`,
which is the reference's file layout.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: A `PeftModel`, or a model adapted by `inject_adapter_in_model`.

Read the values from here instead of `model.state_dict()` —
keyed as that would be.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: The adapter to extract.

raises.description: `model` holds no adapter named `adapter_name`.
The adapter was merged or unloaded, so no LoRA layer is left.
`state_dict` lacks one of the adapter's tensors.

examples:
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model, get_peft_model_state_dict
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 4), nn.Linear(4, 2))
>>> peft = get_peft_model(net, LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"]))
>>> sorted(get_peft_model_state_dict(peft))
['base_model.model.0.lora_A.weight', 'base_model.model.0.lora_B.weight']

members.name: set_peft_model_state_dict
members.signature: set_peft_model_state_dict(model: nn.Module, peft_model_state_dict: Mapping[str, Tensor], adapter_name: str = 'default')
members.summary: Load an adapter's tensors, keyed as an adapter file keys them, into `model`.
members.extended:
Each key is mapped back to where the tensor lives in memory (the
adapter name put back in) and copied into the existing parameter,
which keeps its dtype, device and identity.  Every key is checked
before anything is copied: one that lands nowhere, or a shape that
differs, raises with the model untouched — an adapter loaded into the
wrong model must not pass for a fresh one.  An adapter tensor the dict
does not supply is reported in a warning and keeps its value.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: A `PeftModel`, or a model adapted by `inject_adapter_in_model`.

parameters.name: peft_model_state_dict
parameters.description: On-disk key to tensor, as `get_peft_model_state_dict` returns.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: The adapter to load into.

returns.description:
What `model.load_state_dict(..., strict=False)` returns, typed as
that method declares it: the `(missing_keys, unexpected_keys)`
named tuple, whose `missing_keys` lists the base parameters (no
adapter file holds them) and whose `unexpected_keys` is empty.

raises.description: A key matches no tensor of the model, or a shape differs.
A value is not a Tensor.

examples:
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import (LoraConfig, get_peft_model,
...                         get_peft_model_state_dict, set_peft_model_state_dict)
>>> make = lambda: get_peft_model(nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 2)),
...                               LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"], init_lora_weights=False))
>>> source, target = make(), make()
>>> _ = set_peft_model_state_dict(target, get_peft_model_state_dict(source))
>>> a = target.base_model.model[0].lora_A["default"].weight
>>> bool((a == source.base_model.model[0].lora_A["default"].weight).all().item())
True

members.summary: Load an adapter that has no task, with its base model.
members.extended:
`AutoPeftModel.from_pretrained(directory)` is for an adapter saved
with no `task_type` — a vision model's, for one, since there is no
image task — whose `adapter_config.json` carries an `auto_mapping`
naming the class of the base model.  An adapter with a task is loaded by
the class of its task (`AutoPeftModelForCausalLM` and the others).

The mapping is data read from a file, and building the model imports
the package it names.  Only packages on `import_allowlist`
(`["lucid.models"]` by default) are imported, and what is found there
must be a class with `from_pretrained` (else `TypeError`).
examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import AutoPeftModel
>>> AutoPeftModel()
Traceback (most recent call last):
    ...
OSError: AutoPeftModel is designed to be instantiated using the `AutoPeftModel.from_pretrained(pretrained_model_name_or_path)` method.

members.summary: How `lucid.peft.get_peft_model` adapts a model with LoRA.
members.extended:
LoRA (Hu et al., 2021, [arXiv:2106.09685](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.09685)) freezes a pretrained weight
$W$ and learns a low-rank update beside it, so a targeted
`nn.Linear` computes $W x + s \, B A x$ with
$A \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_{in}}$,
$B \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{out} \times r}$ and scale
$s = \alpha / r$ (or $\alpha / \sqrt{r}$ with rsLoRA).

Field names, defaults and `adapter_config.json` are the reference
adapter library's.  Every field is keyword-only.

parameters.name: task_type
parameters.description: The task the adapter is for (metadata; see `TaskType`).

parameters.name: peft_type
parameters.description: Always `PeftType.LORA`; filled in when omitted.

parameters.name: auto_mapping
parameters.description:
The class of the base model, `{"base_model_class": name,
"parent_library": module}` — what `AutoPeftModel*` rebuilds the
base with.  `PeftModel.save_pretrained` writes it.

parameters.name: base_model_name_or_path
parameters.description: Name of the model the adapter was trained on (metadata).

parameters.name: revision
parameters.description: Revision of that model (metadata).

parameters.name: inference_mode
parameters.description: Freeze the adapter too, for inference.

parameters.name: target_modules
parameters.description:
The `nn.Linear` modules to adapt.  A list matches a module whose
dotted name equals an entry or ends with `"." + entry`; a string
is a regular expression the whole name must match; `"all-linear"`
selects every `nn.Linear` except the output head and any layer
whose weight is shared with another module.  Required: there is
no per-architecture default.

parameters.name: exclude_modules
parameters.description: Modules never adapted, matched like `target_modules`.

parameters.name: modules_to_save
parameters.description:
Modules trained in full beside the adapter (a classifier head);
a trainable copy is kept and saved with it, the original stays.
An entry matches a module whose dotted name equals it or ends
with `"." + entry` — on a dot boundary, so `classifier` does
not also catch `pre_classifier` as the reference's bare suffix
test does.  Nothing inside these modules is adapted.

parameters.name: layers_to_transform
parameters.description:
Adapt only these layer indices (the number after the layer list's
name, `transformer.h.3.attn` → 3).  Applies to modules matched
by suffix; one named in full is adapted regardless.  The index is
the reference's current rule: the first (outer) `<list>.<n>.` in
the name, so `encoder.layers.0.blocks.1.qkv` is layer 0.  A
layer list at the model's root (`h.3.attn`) is indexed too,
where the reference finds no index without a `layers_pattern`.

parameters.name: layers_pattern
r
parameters.description: Rank of the update.

parameters.name: lora_alpha
parameters.description: $\alpha$ in the scale.

parameters.name: lora_dropout
parameters.description: Dropout on the update's input, in `[0, 1)`.

parameters.name: fan_in_fan_out
parameters.description:
For bases that store their weight `(in, out)`.  `nn.Linear`
does not, so `True` warns and is reset to `False`.

parameters.name: bias
parameters.description:
Which biases also train: none, every parameter named `bias`, or
only the biases of the adapted layers.

parameters.name: use_rslora
parameters.description: Scale by $\alpha / \sqrt{r}$ (Kalajdzievski, 2023).

parameters.name: init_lora_weights
parameters.description:
`True`: Kaiming-uniform $A$ (`a = \sqrt 5`) and zero
$B$, so the adapted model starts as the base.
`"gaussian"`: $A \sim \mathcal N(0, 1/r^2)$, zero
$B$.  `False`: both keep `nn.Linear`'s initialisation
(the update is non-zero from the start — for tests).

parameters.name: rank_pattern
parameters.description: Per-module rank overrides, keyed by name or regex suffix.

parameters.name: alpha_pattern
parameters.description: Per-module $\alpha$ overrides, keyed the same way.

parameters.name: use_dora
parameters.description: DoRA; not implemented in v1, `True` raises.

raises.description: A field holds a value of the wrong type.
A field is out of range or two fields conflict.
`use_dora=True` or an initialisation v1 lacks.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig
>>> config = LoraConfig(r=4, lora_alpha=8, target_modules=["q_proj", "v_proj"])
>>> sorted(config.target_modules), config.peft_type
(['q_proj', 'v_proj'], <PeftType.LORA: 'LORA'>)
>>> LoraConfig.from_dict(config.to_dict()) == config
True

members.name: LoraModel
members.signature: LoraModel(model: nn.Module, config: LoraConfig, adapter_name: str = 'default')

methods.name: disable_adapter_layers
methods.summary: Run the base model alone: LoRA updates off, original `modules_to_save`.
methods.extended:
With `bias` other than `"none"` the trained biases are base
parameters and stay as trained, so the output is not the base
model's; a warning says so.

methods.name: add_weighted_adapter
methods.signature: add_weighted_adapter(adapters: list[str], weights: list[float], adapter_name: str, combination_type: _CombinationType = 'svd', svd_rank: int | None = None, svd_clamp: float | None = None, svd_full_matrices: bool = True, svd_driver: str | None = None, density: float | None = None, majority_sign_method: Literal['total', 'frequency'] = 'total')
methods.summary: Add an adapter that is a weighted combination of existing ones.
methods.extended:
The new adapter is frozen and inactive, like any added adapter, and
has $\alpha = r$, so its scale is 1 and the weights live in
its matrices.  It targets the union of the sources' modules; a
layer one source does not reach combines the sources it has.

parameters.name: adapters
parameters.description: Names of the adapters to combine.

parameters.name: weights
parameters.description: One weight per adapter; negative weights subtract.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: Name of the new adapter.

parameters.name: combination_type
parameters.description:
`"svd"`: the rank-`svd_rank` truncation of
$\sum_i w_i s_i B_i A_i$, the nearest rank-`r` update to
the exact sum.  `"cat"`: the exact sum, stacked, at the sum of
the sources' ranks.  `"linear"`: weights `A` and `B` apart
(adding cross terms $B_i A_j$); the sources share a rank.
With one adapter every type is `"linear"`.  The TIES / DARE /
magnitude-prune types of the reference raise `NotImplementedError`.

parameters.name: svd_rank
parameters.description: Rank of an `"svd"` result; the largest source rank by default.

parameters.name: svd_clamp
parameters.description:
A quantile in `[0, 1]`; `"svd"` factors are clamped to the
symmetric range holding that share of their values.

parameters.name: svd_full_matrices
parameters.description: Whether the SVD computes full `U` / `Vh`.

parameters.name: svd_driver
parameters.description: The SVD routine; `lucid.linalg.svd` accepts `None` only.

parameters.name: density
parameters.description: For the TIES / DARE types; unused by the ones implemented.

parameters.name: majority_sign_method
parameters.description: For the TIES types; unused by the ones implemented.

raises.description:
The name is taken, a source does not exist, the weights do not
match the sources, they cannot be combined that way (`"linear"`
needs one rank; two train one `modules_to_save` module), or
`combination_type` is unknown.
`combination_type` is in the TIES / DARE family.

examples:
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, LoraModel
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(6, 5))
>>> config = LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"], init_lora_weights=False)
>>> lora = LoraModel(net, config, adapter_name="a")
>>> lora.add_adapter("b", config)
>>> lora.add_weighted_adapter(["a", "b"], [0.5, 0.5], "mix", combination_type="cat")
>>> net[0].r["mix"]
4

members.summary: A model with LoRA layers put into it, and the tools to take them out.
members.extended:
Construction replaces each module `config` selects with a
`lucid.peft.tuners.lora.Linear` around it and each
`modules_to_save` entry with a frozen-original / trainable-copy
pair, then freezes every other parameter.  The model is changed in
place and kept as `model`; a public name this wrapper lacks is
read from it.  `config` itself is not changed: `peft_config`
holds a copy, with `"all-linear"` spelled out as the names it chose.

The model can hold any number of adapters, each under its own name:
`add_adapter` puts another beside the first (frozen and inactive),
`set_adapter` chooses which one — or which several — the forward pass
applies, `add_weighted_adapter` makes one out of others and
`delete_adapter` removes one.  `active_adapter` is the name, or the
list of names, in use.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: The model to adapt.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: What to adapt and how.

parameters.name: adapter_name
parameters.description: Name of the adapter, the key in every `lora_A` / `lora_B`.

raises.description:
No module matches `target_modules`, a match is not an
`nn.Linear`, or `modules_to_save` matches nothing.

A match is a layer type the reference adapts but lucid.peft does not
(`nn.Embedding`, convolutions, `nn.MultiheadAttention`), or the
model already holds adapter layers (wrap it once; add adapters
with `add_adapter`).

examples:
>>> import lucid.nn as nn
>>> from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, LoraModel
>>> net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(8, 8), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(8, 2))
>>> lora = LoraModel(net, LoraConfig(r=2, target_modules=["0"]))
>>> lora.targeted_module_names
['0']
>>> net[0].base_layer.weight.requires_grad, net[0].lora_A["default"].weight.requires_grad
(False, True)
>>> lora.add_adapter("other", LoraConfig(r=4, target_modules=["0"]))
>>> lora.active_adapters, sorted(lora.peft_config)
(['default'], ['default', 'other'])
>>> lora.set_adapter("other")
>>> lora.active_adapters, net[0].lora_A["default"].weight.requires_grad
(['other'], False)
>>> lora.unload() is net, type(net[0]) is nn.Linear
(True, True)

extended:
Fine-tuning a pretrained model end to end updates, stores and ships every
weight.  LoRA (Hu et al., 2021) freezes them and learns, beside each
chosen `nn.Linear`, a rank-$r$ update $s\,BA$ — on GPT-2
small's `c_attn` at $r = 8$, 294,912 parameters, 0.24 % of the
model — so a fine-tune is trained, saved and swapped as a few megabytes.

The API and the adapter file format are the reference adapter library's,
names and defaults included, so a script written for it reads the same
and an adapter directory moves between the two:

from lucid.peft import LoraConfig, PeftConfig, PeftModel, get_peft_model

config = LoraConfig(r=8, lora_alpha=16, target_modules=["c_attn"],
                        task_type="CAUSAL_LM")
    model = get_peft_model(base_model, config)    # base_model changed in place
    model.print_trainable_parameters()
    ...                                            # train: only the adapter learns
    model.save_pretrained("my-adapter")            # adapter_config.json + adapter_model.safetensors

PeftConfig.from_pretrained("my-adapter").base_model_name_or_path  # which base it needs
    model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(fresh_base_model, "my-adapter")
    merged = model.merge_and_unload()              # a plain model again, adapter folded in

Each method is a config class, a tuner and its layer classes, registered
by `PeftType` as they are defined (`lucid.peft.tuners._base`); the
entry points above dispatch on the method a config or a file names.

What a LoRA layer guarantees:

* **The base is untouched until merged.**  The wrapped `nn.Linear` is
  kept as `base_layer` with its own `Parameter` objects — not
  copies — so an optimizer built earlier, a tied embedding and Core ML's
  identity-keyed weight sharing all still see them, and with the
  default initialisation ($B = 0$) the adapted model's output is
  the base model's, bit for bit.
* **Only the adapter trains.**  Every other parameter is frozen; the
  `bias` option and `modules_to_save` add biases and whole modules.
* **A half-precision base gets a float32 adapter**, computed in float32
  and cast back to the base's output dtype.
* **Merging refuses a shared weight.**  Folding the update into a weight
  another module also uses (a tied LM head) would change that module;
  `merge_and_unload` raises instead.

A model holds any number of adapters, each under its own name:

model.add_adapter("style", LoraConfig(r=4, target_modules=["c_attn"]))
    model.set_adapter("style")                     # compute with — and train — this one
    model.add_weighted_adapter(["default", "style"], [0.7, 0.3], "mix")
    model.save_pretrained("adapters")              # "default" in adapters/, "style" in adapters/style/
    model.load_adapter("adapters/style", "style-again")

The model class follows the task: `get_peft_model` returns a
`PeftModelForCausalLM` for `task_type="CAUSAL_LM"` (and the matching
`PeftModelFor...` class for the other tasks, which also train a
classification or question-answering head), and a config with no
`target_modules` takes the default for the base model's `model_type`.
An adapter directory that names its base model reopens in one call:

model = AutoPeftModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("my-adapter")

lucid.peft adapts `nn.Linear` only.  Asking for more — an embedding or
convolution target, DoRA, a TIES / DARE weighted adapter, an adapter file
of another method — raises `NotImplementedError` rather than doing less
than asked.  Adapters are read from a local directory; hub ids are not
resolved.
